quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "I work at the hospital." She said that she _____.
quests.sentence: Direct: "I work at the hospital." She said that she _____.
quests.hint: In reported speech, present simple ('work') shifts back to past simple ('worked').
quests.explanation: When reporting past speech, present simple shifts to past simple. 'I work' becomes 'she worked' - the reporting verb 'said' triggers the tense backshift.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "We are leaving tomorrow." They said that they _____.
quests.sentence: Direct: "We are leaving tomorrow." They said that they _____.
quests.hint: Present continuous shifts to past continuous; 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.
quests.explanation: Reported speech requires two changes: 'are leaving' (present continuous) shifts to 'were leaving' (past continuous), and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day' since the reporting happens later.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "She has finished the report." He said that she _____.
quests.sentence: Direct: "She has finished the report." He said that she _____.
quests.hint: Present perfect ('has finished') shifts back to past perfect ('had finished') in reported speech.
quests.explanation: In reported speech, the present perfect ('has finished') shifts back to the past perfect ('had finished'). The event is now reported as having already been completed at the time of speaking.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "They bought a new house." She told me that they _____.
quests.sentence: Direct: "They bought a new house." She told me that they _____.
quests.hint: Past simple ('bought') shifts to past perfect ('had bought') in reported speech.
quests.explanation: When the reporting verb is past ('told'), the direct speech's past simple ('bought') shifts to past perfect ('had bought'). This shows the buying happened even further back in time.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "I saw her at the market." He said that he _____ at the market.
quests.sentence: Direct: "I saw her at the market." He said that he _____ at the market.
quests.hint: Past simple ('saw') shifts to past perfect ('had seen') in reported speech.
quests.explanation: Past simple in direct speech shifts to past perfect in reported speech. 'I saw' becomes 'he had seen', placing the event further in the past relative to the reporting moment.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "We were watching TV." She said that they _____.
quests.sentence: Direct: "We were watching TV." She said that they _____.
quests.hint: Past continuous ('were watching') shifts to past perfect continuous ('had been watching').
quests.explanation: Past continuous in direct speech shifts to past perfect continuous in reported speech. 'Were watching' becomes 'had been watching', keeping the continuous nature while moving the event back in time.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "You should rest." The doctor said that I _____ rest.
quests.sentence: Direct: "You should rest." The doctor said that I _____ rest.
quests.hint: 'Should' does not change in reported speech.
quests.explanation: 'Should' is one of the modals that stays the same in reported speech - it does not shift to another form. 'Must', 'might', 'could', and 'would' also remain unchanged.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "I can help you." She said that she _____ help me.
quests.sentence: Direct: "I can help you." She said that she _____ help me.
quests.hint: 'Can' shifts to 'could' in reported speech.
quests.explanation: 'Can' is one of the modals that does shift in reported speech: 'can' → 'could'. This is different from 'should', 'might', 'could', and 'would', which stay the same.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "They will arrive at noon." She said that they _____ arrive at noon.
quests.sentence: Direct: "They will arrive at noon." She said that they _____ arrive at noon.
quests.hint: 'Will' shifts to 'would' in reported speech.
quests.explanation: 'Will' shifts to 'would' in reported speech - this is one of the most important modal backshifts to remember. 'Will → would' parallels the same relationship as the second conditional.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "Are you coming?" He asked me _____.
quests.sentence: Direct: "Are you coming?" He asked me _____.
options: whether I was coming or not
quests.hint: Reported yes/no questions use 'if/whether' + subject + verb (no inversion, tense shifted).
quests.explanation: Reported yes/no questions use 'if' or 'whether' and remove the inversion. 'Are you coming?' → 'if I was coming'. The question mark is also dropped because it is now a statement structure.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "Did she pass the exam?" He asked me _____.
quests.sentence: Direct: "Did she pass the exam?" He asked me _____.
options: if she had passed the exam
if she has passed the exam
quests.correctAnswer: if she had passed the exam
quests.hint: Past simple → past perfect; use 'if' + statement word order (no inversion).
quests.explanation: Reported questions never use question word order. 'Did she pass?' → 'if she had passed' - past simple becomes past perfect, and the auxiliary 'did' disappears entirely.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "Have they finished?" She wanted to know _____.
quests.sentence: Direct: "Have they finished?" She wanted to know _____.
quests.hint: Use 'whether/if' + subject + verb (no inversion); present perfect shifts to past perfect.
quests.explanation: 'Whether' (or 'if') introduces reported yes/no questions. 'Have they finished?' → 'whether they had finished' - inversion disappears, and the present perfect shifts to past perfect.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "Where do you live?" She asked me _____.
quests.sentence: Direct: "Where do you live?" She asked me _____.
quests.hint: Reported wh-questions keep the question word but remove inversion and shift the tense.
quests.explanation: Reported wh-questions keep 'where' but switch to statement word order and shift the tense. 'Where do you live?' → 'where I lived'. 'Do' disappears; 'live' shifts to 'lived'.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "What time will the train leave?" He asked _____.
quests.sentence: Direct: "What time will the train leave?" He asked _____.
options: what time the train would leave
what time will the train leave
quests.correctAnswer: what time the train would leave
quests.hint: Keep 'what time', remove inversion, shift 'will' → 'would'.
quests.explanation: The wh-phrase 'what time' stays, but the question inversion disappears and 'will' shifts to 'would'. 'What time will the train leave?' → 'what time the train would leave'.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "Why didn't you call me?" She asked him _____.
quests.sentence: Direct: "Why didn't you call me?" She asked him _____.
quests.hint: 'Why' stays; statement word order; 'didn't' → 'hadn't' (past perfect); pronoun shifts.
quests.explanation: Reported wh-question: 'why' stays, inversion disappears, 'didn't call' shifts to 'hadn't called' (past perfect), and pronouns shift from 'you → he' and 'me → her'.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "Open the window." He told me _____.
quests.sentence: Direct: "Open the window." He told me _____.
quests.hint: Reported commands use 'tell/ask + object + to + base verb'.
quests.explanation: Commands in reported speech use 'tell/ask + person + to + base verb'. 'Open' becomes 'to open'. There is no 'that', no tense shift needed, and no question structure.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "Don't touch that." She told me _____ that.
quests.sentence: Direct: "Don't touch that." She told me _____ that.
quests.hint: Negative reported commands: 'tell + person + not to + base verb'.
quests.explanation: Negative reported commands use 'not to + base verb'. 'Don't touch that' → 'not to touch that'. 'To not touch' is less standard, though sometimes acceptable; 'not to touch' is the preferred form.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "Please be quiet." The teacher asked us _____.
quests.sentence: Direct: "Please be quiet." The teacher asked us _____.
quests.hint: 'Please' is dropped; command becomes 'ask + us + to be quiet'.
quests.explanation: When reporting polite commands with 'please', the word 'please' is dropped. The structure becomes 'ask + object + to + base verb': 'asked us to be quiet'.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: He said, "I'll see you tomorrow." He said he would see me _____.
quests.sentence: He said, "I'll see you tomorrow." He said he would see me _____.
quests.hint: In reported speech, 'tomorrow' shifts to 'the next day' or 'the following day' - not 'tomorrow'.
quests.explanation: 'Tomorrow' in direct speech must change in reported speech because it refers to a time relative to when it was spoken. 'The next day' is the standard shift. 'The following day' is also correct.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: She said, "I was here yesterday." She said she had been there _____.
quests.sentence: She said, "I was here yesterday." She said she had been there _____.
quests.hint: 'Yesterday' shifts to 'the day before' or 'the previous day' in reported speech.
quests.explanation: 'Yesterday' shifts to 'the day before' (or 'the previous day') when reported later. Also note that 'here' shifts to 'there' because the place reference changes too.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: He said, "I saw her last week." He said he had seen her _____.
quests.sentence: He said, "I saw her last week." He said he had seen her _____.
quests.hint: 'Last week' shifts to 'the week before' or 'the previous week'.
quests.explanation: 'Last week' in direct speech becomes 'the week before' or 'the previous week' in reported speech. 'A week ago' could work in some contexts but is less standard for reported speech.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: "I'm going to quit my job," she told her friend.
quests.sentence: "I'm going to quit my job," she told her friend.
options: She told her friend that she was going to quit her job.
She told her friend that she is going to quit her job.
She said her friend that she was going to quit her job.
She told to her friend that she was going to quit her job.
quests.correctAnswer: She told her friend that she was going to quit her job.
quests.hint: Use 'tell + object' (not 'tell to'); shift 'am going' → 'was going'; shift 'my' → 'her'.
quests.explanation: 'Tell' takes a direct object: 'told her friend', not 'told to her friend'. 'I'm going' shifts to 'she was going', and 'my job' shifts to 'her job'.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: "Don't worry about me," he said to her.
quests.sentence: "Don't worry about me," he said to her.
options: He told her not to worry about him.
He said her not to worry about him.
He told her don't worry about him.
He said to her not to worry about her.
quests.correctAnswer: He told her not to worry about him.
quests.hint: Negative command: 'told her not to worry'; pronouns shift 'me' → 'him'.
quests.explanation: 'Tell + object + not to + base verb' reports negative commands. 'Say' cannot take a direct person object ('say her' is wrong). Pronouns shift: 'me' becomes 'him' when referring to the speaker.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: "Have you ever been to Japan?" she asked him.
quests.sentence: "Have you ever been to Japan?" she asked him.
options: She asked him if he had ever been to Japan.
She asked him have you ever been to Japan.
She asked him if he has ever been to Japan.
She asked him if had he ever been to Japan.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked him if he had ever been to Japan.
quests.hint: Reported yes/no question: 'if' + statement order + past perfect; pronoun 'you → he'.
quests.explanation: Reported yes/no questions use 'if/whether' + statement word order. Present perfect shifts to past perfect: 'have you been' → 'if he had been'. No inversion ('if had he' is wrong).

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Choose the correct sentence:
quests.sentence: Choose the correct sentence:
options: She told me that the meeting was cancelled.
She said me that the meeting was cancelled.
She told that the meeting was cancelled.
She said to me that the meeting was cancelled.
quests.correctAnswer: She told me that the meeting was cancelled.
quests.hint: 'Tell' must have a person object directly after it: 'told me'; 'said' uses 'said to me' or 'said that'.
quests.explanation: 'Tell' always takes a direct object: 'told me / told him / told us'. You cannot say 'told that'. 'Say' never takes a direct person object - use 'said to me' or 'said that'.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: He _____ us not to use our phones in class.
quests.sentence: He _____ us not to use our phones in class.
quests.hint: 'Tell + object + not to + verb' - 'say' can't take a direct person object.
quests.explanation: Reported negative commands require 'tell + person + not to + base verb'. 'Say' cannot directly precede a person object, so 'said us' is wrong. 'Spoke/talked' don't fit this structure at all.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: She _____ that she would be late.
quests.sentence: She _____ that she would be late.
quests.hint: 'Said that ...' without a person object - 'told' must always have a person object.
quests.explanation: When there is no person object ('told me/him/her'), use 'said'. 'Said that she would be late' is correct. 'Told that ...' (without a person object) is grammatically wrong in standard English.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "I must submit the form today." She said she _____ the form that day.
quests.sentence: Direct: "I must submit the form today." She said she _____ the form that day.
quests.hint: 'Must' shifts to 'had to' in reported speech.
quests.explanation: 'Must' is an exception: it shifts to 'had to' (not 'musted') in reported speech. 'Would' and 'should' don't capture the obligation meaning of 'must'.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "We might go camping." They said they _____ camping.
quests.sentence: Direct: "We might go camping." They said they _____ camping.
quests.hint: 'Might' does not change in reported speech - it stays as 'might'.
quests.explanation: 'Might' is one of the modals that stays the same when reported. 'May' also sometimes shifts to 'might', but 'might' itself never changes.

quests.instruction: Turn the statement into a question.
quests.question: Direct: "Come back tomorrow." She told him to _____.
quests.sentence: Direct: "Come back tomorrow." She told him to _____.
options: to come back the next day
quests.hint: Reported command = 'told him to + base verb'; 'tomorrow' shifts to 'the next day'.
quests.explanation: Reported commands use 'to + base verb'. The time adverb 'tomorrow' shifts to 'the next day'. 'To come back the next day' has a redundant 'to' before it - the 'to' is already included in 'told him to come back'.
